A dry pattern will remain over the Marianas through tonight. To the
north, Invest 93W was downgraded to medium by the Joint Typhoon 
Warning Center (JTWC), and is expected to move northeast to east- 
northeast. As 93W progresses, convection to the west of the Marianas
looks to progress eastward, increasing POPs (Probability of 
Precipitation) across the Marianas. This batch of showers is 
expected to move through over the weekend, with a brief dry period 
returning for Monday. Then, Invest 92W, currently north of Kosrae, is
expected to approach the region. As of now, most of the models agree
that Invest 92W will move through as only a weak disturbance, or 
possibly a weak tropical depression, with only the GFS and ECMWF 
deterministic models showing a stronger system. Therefore, it looks 
like a wetter pattern is in store for the Marianas Tuesday through 
most of the week, with gusty winds in showers. Invest 92W will 
continue to be monitored closely for any changes to expected 
development. 

Marine/Surf...
Latest WaveWatch model guidance shows the west swell has subsided
enough to allow surf to fall below hazardous levels along west 
facing reefs, also resulting in the rip current risk dropping to 
moderate. Therefore, the High Surf Advisory and High Rip Current 
Risk statement were both allowed to expire at 4 PM this afternoon.
Seas and wind look to continue to slowly subside over the next few
days.

Tropical Systems...
A broad, weak circulation, Invest 92W, is centered north of Kosrae 
near 8.7N 161.7E, within broad troughing extending SE from north of 
Weno, Chuuk to beyond the Equator near 175E. 92W is moving slowly
west and remains sub-low, meaning no development is expected over 
the next few days. 92W, along with the trough, is producing heavy
convection across Chuuk, Pohnpei, and Kosrae States. Invest 92W will
continue to move west-northwest over the coming days with little or 
no change in intensity. As of now, most of the models agree that 
Invest 92W will move through the Marianas as only a weak disturbance,
or possibly a weak tropical depression, with only the GFS and ECMWF 
deterministic models showing a stronger system. The trough looks to 
strengthen a bit over the coming days and the monsoon trough may 
reestablish farther south along this trough over the next week or so.

A more organized circulation, Invest 93W, is centered south of Iwo 
To near 22.3N 140.7E and is moving east-northeast. 93W was downgraded
to medium by JTWC, meaning development into a significant tropical 
cyclone is likely, but beyond the next 24 hours. Satellite shows a 
compact Low-Level Circulation Center (LLCC) with increasing 
convection near the center. The latest ASCAT analysis shows fresh to 
strong winds around the circulation with stronger winds seen a bit 
farther south in the monsoonal flow. Conditions remain favorable for 
development of Invest 93W, with weak vertical wind shear, good upper-
level outflow and warm sea surface temperatures. This has been a 
favored location lately for development of weak, short-lived tropical
cyclones moving northeast.

For more information on Invest 93W, please see bulletins issued by 
JTWC under WMO header ABPW10 PGTW and WTPN21 PGTW.

Eastern Micronesia...
Invest 92W continues to meander north of Kosrae with little change in
intensity. Moderate to strong northwesterly convergence west of 92W 
continues to induce numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms 
across Pohnpei and Kosrae. Model guidance indicates intensification
of the westerly convergence beginning early next week, so widespread
locally heavy showers, isolated thunderstorms, and gusty winds are 
possible for Pohnpei and Kosrae. A Special Weather Statement (SPS) 
was issued to address the heightened flooding and mudslide potentials
at least through Wednesday.

Majuro remains on the outskirts of the unsettled weather pattern, so
scattered showers and on-and-off isolated thunderstorms are
forecasted through next week. Swell heights will hover 3 to 4 ft, 
shifting from the southeast to the southwest over the course of the 
forecast period. Light to gentle southerly winds will shift to the 
west through early next week, eventually ending up northerly around 
midweek should 92W move away to the north-northwest.

A High Surf Advisory is in effect for south-facing reefs of Kosrae
through early Tuesday morning. In the event that the south swell
remains elevated, the advisory may need to be extended. Although
there are no current WWAs in effect for Pohnpei, marine interests
should stay updated with the forecast and heed local emergency
management advice as the swells build through the middle of next
week.

Western Micronesia...
Satellite imagery shows isolated showers and partly cloudy skies
across Palau and Yap, and cloudy skies with widespread showers and
isolated thunderstorms across Chuuk. Altimetry and buoy data show
combined seas are between 3 and 6 feet.
